title: Mean reversion: a repeated excursion is suppressed until the latch re-arms
purpose: Staying beyond the entry threshold, or between the bands, never repeats a request; a constant window re-arms the latch and z is then unavailable (not zero).

provenance.derived_by: by hand, from the strategy document and the fixture bars; not copied from any run of the tool
sources: docs/strategies/mean_reversion.md section 4 (the latch: no repeats, constant window)
derivation: bar 5: window 10 10 6 2, mean 7, variance 11, z^2 = 25/11 = 2.27 >= 1.5^2 = 2.25 so z = -1.5076 is beyond the entry on the requested side: no repeat (excursion_already_requested)
bars 6-8: z = -1.0528, -0.7276, -0.5774, all strictly between the re-arm 0.5 and the entry 1.5: nothing, latch unchanged
bar 9: window 1 1 1 1 is constant: nothing, z unavailable, latch re-armed
bar 10: window 1 1 1 10, mean 13/4, variance 243/16, z = sqrt(3) = 1.732 >= 1.5 and latch neutral: Sell (event_index 9)

irrational_double.why: irrational value, rounded to 17 significant digits; the C++ computes it in IEEE double (about 1e-16 relative), so a few ulps of a value below 40 is about 1e-14. 1e-12 leaves two orders of margin and is far below any difference that could change a decision here
